frameworks.name: comparative_advantage
frameworks.notes: WARNING: Ricardian comparative advantage poorly explains military drone trade — state security alignment dominates price. France's military UAV base (Thales, Dassault nEUROn, Taranis JV heritage, Delair OSKAR loitering munitions) is real but Turkey (Baykar TB2/Akıncı) and China (Wing Loong, CH series) outcompete on price and permissiveness. French exports face MTCR/EU/end-use conditionality — a structural barrier, not a productivity signal.

frameworks.name: gravity
frameworks.notes: Gravity further weakened: arms trade follows alliance structures, not GDP/distance alone. Use CAGE-style political distance as a better proxy if team adopts it.

products.name: military_drones
products.notes: Same HS code as commercial drones — customs data will NOT separate them. Team must decide: either merge products 3 and 4, or source from SIPRI Arms Transfers Database instead of COMTRADE. Flagged for methodology decision.

countries.name: Philippines
countries.notes: South China Sea pressure driving UAV demand; US ally wary of Chinese hardware; France a politically acceptable alternative supplier; minimal French arms link to date.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.notes: Non-aligned buyer diversifying from Chinese systems; existing French defense relationship (Rafale, submarines) — strong 'new link on existing channel' candidate.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.notes: Skewed to Turkish/Israeli suppliers; French defense ties growing; test of whether France can enter a Turkish-dominated drone market.

trade_links.source: estimate — no known French military UAV deliveries to Philippines
estimate — French sales to Indonesia are Rafale/submarines, not UAVs; verify via SIPRI
